ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Hatshepsut

code.originalText: New patient visit for a painful swollen jaw from a suspected dental abscess, with diabetes found on screening; urgent oral and maxillofacial surgery referral

text.paragraph: New patient visit for a painful swollen jaw from a suspected dental abscess, with diabetes found on screening; urgent oral and maxillofacial surgery referral [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Her jaw is swollen and throbbing and she cannot chew; she wants it treated quickly so she can keep her public engagements. [S]
She was surprised to hear she has diabetes and wants a plan she can keep with her schedule, without being lectured about her weight. [S]
Her knees hurt on stairs at the building sites. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Hatshepsut was a daughter of the king Thutmose I and became the chief queen of Thutmose II. [D]

After the death of Thutmose II she acted as guardian and regent for the young Thutmose III, her nephew and stepson; by his seventh regnal year she had taken the public role of a king, while still referred to with feminine forms. [D]
She claimed to have been born of a union between her mother and the god Amun-Ra, and looked to her father Thutmose I as the source of her kingship. [D]
Her birth year is not recorded. An age of about 50 at death, suggested by study of the mummy identified as hers, would place her birth about 1507 BC; this is a rough estimate. [R]

text.paragraph: 8 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.

list.item: Painful swelling of the left lower jaw for four days, after a throbbing toothache for three weeks under a broken lower left molar; low-grade temperature, no trismus, no swelling of the floor of the mouth or neck; dental abscess suspected: active, confirmed [S]

Type 2 diabetes found on screening (hemoglobin A1c 7.6% with a random glucose of 212 mg/dL from the same sample), with thirst and waking at night to pass urine; normal kidney function and urine albumin: active, confirmed [S]
Obesity, class 2 (BMI 36.3), with type 2 diabetes and knee osteoarthritis; she wants to feel stronger and move more easily: active, confirmed [S]
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees: pain on stairs and after standing, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus, no effusion; a clinical diagnosis without imaging: active, confirmed [S]

Dental pain and infection safety today: ibuprofen 400 mg with acetaminophen 1 g, alternating, for up to a week, and no opioid; no antibiotic, because the swelling is localized, there is no fever above 38 °C, no trismus and no spread, and drainage is arranged within 24 hours; go to the emergency department at once for swelling spreading to the eye, the floor of the mouth or the neck, difficulty swallowing or breathing, trouble opening the mouth, or a fever. Guideline: Evidence-based clinical practice guideline on antibiotic use for the urgent management of pulpal- and periapical-related dental pain and intraoral swelling (2019); Evidence-based clinical practice guideline for the pharmacologic management of acute dental pain in adolescents, adults, and older adults (2024) [S]

Urgent oral and maxillofacial surgery consultation within 24 hours for imaging, drainage of the abscess and extraction or other definitive treatment of the broken molar, with an assessment of her gums. Guideline: Evidence-based clinical practice guideline on antibiotic use for the urgent management of pulpal- and periapical-related dental pain and intraoral swelling (2019); Scientific evidence on the links between periodontal diseases and diabetes: Consensus report and guidelines of the joint workshop on periodontal diseases and diabetes by the International Diabetes Federation and the European Federation of Periodontology (2018) [S]

Type 2 diabetes: metformin extended-release, started slowly; diabetes self-management education and medical nutrition therapy in the clinic's program; A1c every three months until at goal; eye screening, a comprehensive foot examination and kidney tests at diagnosis and yearly; blood pressure goal below 130/80; sick-day rules for metformin; endocrinology only if the A1c is not at goal by six months. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Section 2, Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes; Section 9, Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment) (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and hyperlipidemia monographs (2026) [S]

Weight and health without stigma: person-first language, weight discussed only with her permission, goals she sets for strength and movement, and the medicines that lower both glucose and weight (GLP-1 receptor agonists) explained for her to consider. Guideline: Obesity and Weight Management for the Prevention and Treatment of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Section 8) (2026) [S]

Knee osteoarthritis: a walking and strengthening program, diclofenac gel as needed, and a cane or knee support for long site visits if helpful; no imaging needed for a clinical diagnosis. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and hyperlipidemia monographs (2026) [S]
Mood screening: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at the end of the episode. Guideline: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to oral and maxillofacial surgery, Rashid Lindqvist-Bello, DDS, ordered 2026-04-14 [S]
